topSpeedMPS.citation: Averaged from two real sources at the same developmental stage: J. Functional Morphology & Kinesiology 2025's Mid-PHV V0 (9.20+/-0.61 m/s, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12821503/) and European Journal of Sport Science 2024's ~13.8/14.8yo on-ice peak speed (male 9.83, female 9.08 m/s, avg 9.455, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11451559/). Average of the two study averages: (9.20+9.455)/2 = 9.3275, rounded to 9.33.

accel0to10mS.citation: J. Functional Morphology & Kinesiology 2025, Mid-PHV 0-10m acceleration: 2.11+/-0.16s. The EJSS study didn't report acceleration, so only the PMC12821503 figure is used here.

avgAccelMPS2.citation: Computed from accel0to10mS via kinematics (d = 0.5*a*t^2, d=10m).

turningRadiusM.citation: No published turning-radius figure exists at any age. Estimated as v^2 / (0.6 * avgAccelMPS2).

stoppingDistanceM.citation: No published stopping-distance figure exists at any age. Estimated as v^2 / (2 * avgAccelMPS2).

reactionDelayS.citation: No ice-hockey or youth-hockey reaction-time study exists at any age. 250-350ms range built from adult non-hockey athlete proxy data (PMC11207928), applied flat across all bands.

passSpeedMPS.citation: No youth ice-hockey pass-velocity study exists. Scaled from the U18 pass-speed reference (18 m/s) by this band's real topSpeedMPS ratio to U18's.

iceDecelerationMPS2.citation: mu*g using Hache's puck-on-ice friction coefficient (~0.1, https://physicsworld.com/a/physics-on-ice/) and standard gravity. Real, age-independent physical constant.
